page.layout: One block of verse in the centre of the page, indented lines alternating; a catchword "Fran-" at the lower right below the last line. Page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p:
Bellísque dulces callida ciuicis
Mutare paces, viribus exteris
Fidens iuuentus, ausa Gallis
Ausa suo est dare iura Regi!
Illúmque amatis vrbibus expulit,
Minata cædes vincláque turpia,
Durífque cedentem procellis
Signa sequi Lotharena iussit.
Sed magna Regis mens violentiam,
Sanósque fortis contudit impetus,
Virésque prouisis minores
Consiliis melior subegit.
Sic sic minantes exitium Ioui
Pallas Gigantes Ægide perdidit:
Quum fulminantem iuuit illa
Consilio potiore patrem.
Non vis furenti profuit impia
Turba, nec Ossa Pelion insitus.
Vis sola conatúsque semper
Mole ruunt propria nefasti.
Nunc fraudulentis hostibus obrutis,
Rex magne, motus discute turbidos:
Pacémque languenti benignus
Perpetuam patria redona.
Nam tota cunctis vrbibus ingemit
Oppressa diris Gallia cladibus,
Tristésque maƈtatis cruenta
Ciuibus ingeminat querelas.

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Some letters in the verse are worn and doubtful; the line "Quum fulminantem iuuit illa" may read "iuuit" or "ieiunit" in the printer's text. The word "Fran-" is a catchword set at the lower right.
